focus: Contraction 'll /l/ (I'll, we'll, it'll) · 'won't' /wəʊnt/ vs 'want' /wɒnt/ · weak 'will' /wl/ · linking 'I'll + verb' · 'shall/'ll' in offers
focus_ar: الاختصار 'll، و 'won't' مقابل 'want'، و 'will' الخفيفة، ووصل I'll بالفعل، والعروض
arabic_challenge: The contracted 'll is just a dark /l/ attached to the pronoun (I'll = /aɪl/), which Arabic learners often expand back to 'I will' or drop entirely. 'Won't' and 'want' are a classic confusion because the vowels /əʊ/ and /ɒ/ both feel foreign.

isolation.instructions: 'Will' contracts to a single /l/ glued to the pronoun: I'll /aɪl/, we'll /wiːl/, he'll /hiːl/, it'll /ɪtl/, they'll /ðeɪl/. It is one syllable — do not say 'I will'.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'will' بتتقلّص لـ /l/ ملزوقة بالضمير: I'll /aɪl/، we'll، he'll. مقطع واحد — متقولش 'I will'.

daily_drills.record_this: I'll call you later and we'll decide together. He'll be here soon, and they'll arrive tomorrow morning.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'I'll'. Is it one syllable that rhymes with 'aisle', not two words?

isolation.instructions: 'Won't' (will not) has the GLIDING /əʊ/ — like 'phone'. 'Want' has the SHORT /ɒ/ — like 'hot'. Mixing them reverses your meaning entirely.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'won't' فيها /əʊ/ المتحركة (زي phone). 'want' فيها /ɒ/ القصيرة (زي hot). الخلط بينهم بيقلب المعنى.

sentence_practice: I want to help but I won't have time.
daily_drills.record_this: I won't be late tonight. I want to help you, but I won't have much time. Don't worry — it won't rain today.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'won't' then 'want'. Does the first glide like 'phone' and the second stay short like 'hot'?

isolation.instructions: When 'will' is not contracted, it is still usually WEAK: 'Will you help?' sounds like 'wl-you-help'. Only stress it for strong promises or contradiction.
isolation.instructions_ar: لما 'will' متتقلّصش، بتفضل خفيفة غالبًا: 'Will you help?' → wl-you-help. مانضغط عليها إلا للوعد القوي.

daily_drills.record_this: Will you help me later? When will they arrive, and what will happen next? I think it will be fine.
daily_drills.self_check: In 'Will you help?', does 'will' stay light, with the stress on 'help'?

isolation.instructions: Glue the contraction to the verb: I'll-GO, we'll-SEE, I'll-HELP. The stress is on the verb. Make on-the-spot decisions sound instant and smooth.
isolation.instructions_ar: الزق الاختصار بالفعل: I'll-GO, we'll-SEE. النبر على الفعل. خلي القرارات اللحظية تبان سريعة وسلسة.

daily_drills.record_this: That box is heavy — I'll help you carry it. OK, I'll take this one. Don't worry, we'll manage, and I'll call you if there's a problem.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'I'll help you' as an instant offer. Is it smooth and fast, stressed on 'help'?

isolation.instructions: Offers and quick decisions use 'll: 'I'll get it', 'I'll pay'. In questions, 'Shall I…?' /ʃəl aɪ/ offers help. Keep both light and friendly, rising at the end for offers.
isolation.instructions_ar: العروض والقرارات السريعة بـ 'll: 'I'll get it'. وفي السؤال 'Shall I…?' لعرض المساعدة. خليهم خفاف وودودين بنغمة صاعدة.

sentence_practice: The phone's ringing — I'll get it.
Shall I help you with that?
daily_drills.record_this: The phone is ringing — I'll get it! Shall I help you with those bags? I'll pay for the taxi, and shall we go now before it rains?
daily_drills.self_check: Do your offers rise gently at the end and sound friendly, not flat?

challenge_sentences: I'll help you and we'll finish quickly.
I won't be late, I promise.
Will you call me when you arrive?
Shall I get the door? I'll pay for lunch.
daily_drills.record_this: Don't worry — I'll help you and we'll finish quickly. I won't be late, I promise. Will you call me when you arrive? Shall I get the door? And I'll pay for lunch today.
daily_drills.self_check: Three checks: 'll is one syllable, 'won't' glides (not 'want'), and 'will you' stays weak.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself making predictions and offers. Then listen back and check each feature.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك وانت بتعمل توقعات وعروض، وبعدين اسمع وراجع كل نقطة.
test_yourself.passage: I think tomorrow will be a good day. The weather won't be too hot, so we'll go to the park. I'll bring some food and you'll bring the drinks. If it rains, we won't stay outside — we'll go to a café instead. Shall I call the others? I'm sure they'll want to come. Don't worry about the cost; I'll pay this time and you'll pay next time. It'll be fun. I won't be late, I promise, and we'll have a great afternoon together.

sounds_to_check.'won't' /əʊ/ vs 'want': won't be, won't stay, won't be late
sounds_to_check.weak 'will': tomorrow will be, they'll want (not WILL)
sounds_to_check.linking 'I'll + verb': I'll BRING, I'll PAY, we'll GO

scoring_guide.90_100: 'll is a clean single syllable, 'won't/want' never merge, offers sound friendly. Ready for week 7.
scoring_guide.70_89: Good; occasional 'I will' where 'I'll' is natural.
scoring_guide.50_69: 'won't' and 'want' still merge, or 'll is dropped. Repeat days 1-2.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-4, gluing each 'll to its verb.

for_arabic_speakers: 'll is a single dark /l/ on the pronoun — 'I'll' rhymes with 'aisle', one syllable.
'won't' glides like 'phone'; 'want' is short like 'hot'. This pair reverses your meaning.
Use 'll for on-the-spot decisions and offers (I'll get it); it makes you sound natural and quick.
'Will you…?' and 'Shall I…?' stay light and rise gently — that is what makes them polite.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
